chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan and Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

The Muhrim (person in Ihram) pays the ransom for the game from wherever he catches it. And whoever wishes to slaughter [the ransom animal] in Mina, let him slaughter wherever he wishes, and likewise in Mecca. It was narrated.

key_terms.اَلْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: Where should a pilgrim in Ihram slaughter the ransom animal for killing game?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *fidyah* (ransom) for killing game while in Ihram, linking the compensation value to the specific location of the catch. It further clarifies the procedural flexibility for the pilgrim, allowing the sacrificial animal to be slaughtered in Mina or Mecca, reflecting the practical jurisprudence of the time. This ruling underscores the balance between ritual sanctity and logistical ease in Shia fiqh.
